_note: The part of an employer's spending on medical treatment and stay abroad (of the employee, a family member, and one attendant) that is excluded from the perquisite: the spending, but "only to the extent permitted by the Reserve Bank of India" (D-112; rulebook PERQ-MEDABROAD-001). The Reserve Bank sets no figure the Act names, so the permitted amount is entered. TY 2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 s.17(2)(f), s.17(3)(a) (Gazette 265620, pp.39–40). TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.17(2) proviso (vi) condition (A), and clause (vii) for a reimbursement (thc.nic.in pp.144–145). MedicalTreatmentAbroadNode takes the excluded amount off the spending; the rest is salary. Every regime: a perquisite is salary.

introducedBy.instrumentCitation: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.17(2) proviso (vi) as last amended by the Finance Act, 2025 (7 of 2025), s.9(b) — which changed only condition (B), the travel threshold; condition (A) stands as substituted by Act 38 of 1993, s.8 (thc.nic.in footnote, not read in the Act)

provenance.sourceDescription: Income-tax Act, 1961 as on thc.nic.in (current to Act 7 of 2019), s.17(2) proviso (vi) and (vii), pp.144–145
provenance.whatToCheck: The Income-tax Act, 1961 text is read in the thc.nic.in consolidation, current to Act 7 of 2019: the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019, the Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 and the interim Finance Act, 2024 are unread for s.17(2) proviso (vi) and clause (vii); the Finance Acts 2020-2023, the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024, the Finance Act, 2025 and the Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025 were read and only the Finance Act, 2025 s.9(b) touches it.
